entities.evidence: Genesis 10:6 lists Cush among Ham’s sons. Here the genealogy identifies him as Nimrod’s father.
אֶת marks Nimrod as the son Cush fathered. The following clause describes Nimrod as a mighty man on the earth.

review.translation: [Cush also|0] [fathered|1] [Nimrod|3,2], [who|4] [began|5] [to be|6] [a mighty man|7] [on the earth|8].

analysis.evidence: Cush is the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’, and אֶת marks Nimrod as the direct object. The verse identifies Cush as Nimrod’s father.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ is prefixed to the personal name כּוּשׁ.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66578:5, 66578:9, 66578:13.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In וְכוּשׁ יָלַד אֶת נִמְרֹד, Cush is the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’, and אֶת marks the proper name נִמְרֹד ‘Nimrod’ as its definite direct object.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Extend the existing Nimrod article’s summary and add Genesis 10:9 as evidence for his reputation as a hunter.
draft.definition: Nimrod, son of Cush, remembered as a mighty hunter before Yahweh.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:8 identifies Nimrod as Cush’s son. In Genesis 10:9, the saying names him as its standard of comparison with the words כְּנִמְרֹד, “like Nimrod.”

analysis.evidence: In וְכוּשׁ יָלַד אֶת נִמְרֹד, אֶת marks Nimrod as the person Cush fathered. The pronoun הוּא then refers back to Nimrod as the one who became mighty on earth. The verse gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Nimrod, the mighty hunter cited in the saying.

analysis.evidence: The first clause names Nimrod as the son Cush fathered. In הוּא הֵחֵל, “he began,” the pronoun picks up Nimrod as the subject of הֵחֵל.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers to Nimrod. The following infinitive לִהְיוֹת supplies the complement of הֵחֵל, giving the reading “he began to be a mighty man on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular. The initial ה is part of the Hiphil stem.

analysis.evidence: In הוּא הֵחֵל לִהְיוֹת גִּבֹּר בָּאָרֶץ, “he began to be a mighty man on the earth,” הֵחֵל expresses the onset, and הְיוֹת links Nimrod to the description גִּבֹּר.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ introduces the Qal infinitive construct הְיוֹת as the complement of הֵחֵל, “he began.”
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: The pronoun הוּא refers to Nimrod. The phrase הֵחֵל לִהְיוֹת גִּבֹּר בָּאָרֶץ says that he began to be a mighty man on earth. The verse leaves the field of his prowess unspecified.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally as the complement of לִהְיוֹת.
